Guide to Student Applications and Admissions

This guide explains how to apply for admission to undergraduate programmes, which documents you will need, how your application will be assessed, and what happens after you receive a decision. Please read it carefully before starting your application.

Before you apply

Check the entry requirements for the programme you are interested in. Requirements usually include minimum marks in specific subjects, proof of language proficiency and, for some courses, a portfolio or entrance test. If you are unsure whether your qualifications are suitable, contact the admissions office before the deadline. Staff can advise you on equivalent qualifications from other boards and countries.

Make a note of all deadlines. Applications received after the closing date may not be considered, and some scholarships have earlier deadlines than the main application.

Completing the application form

Applications are submitted through the online portal. Create an account using a valid email address that you check regularly, because all communication about your application will be sent there. Fill in your personal details exactly as they appear on your identity documents. Enter your educational history in order, starting with your most recent qualification.

The personal statement is your opportunity to explain why you want to study the programme and what you will bring to it. Write clearly and honestly, give specific examples of your interests and achievements, and check your spelling and grammar before submitting.

Supporting documents

You will need to upload scanned copies of the following documents: mark sheets and certificates for completed qualifications, a valid identity document, a recent passport-size photograph, proof of language proficiency where required, and a reference letter from a teacher or employer. Each file must be in PDF or JPEG format and no larger than two megabytes.

If any document is not in English, please provide a certified translation along with the original. Applications with missing documents cannot be assessed, so check that every required item has been uploaded before you submit.

Application fee and payment

A non-refundable application fee is payable when you submit your form. You can pay online by debit card, credit card or net banking. Keep the payment receipt, as you may be asked to provide it if there is a problem with your application. Fee waivers are available for applicants who meet certain income criteria; details and the waiver request form are available on the admissions website.

Assessment and selection

Once the deadline has passed, applications are reviewed by the admissions committee for each programme. The committee considers your academic record, personal statement, reference and, where relevant, test results or portfolio. Some programmes invite shortlisted applicants for an interview, which may be held in person or online.

Decisions are usually released within six to eight weeks of the closing date. You will receive an email asking you to log in to the portal to view your decision.

Offers and acceptance

If you receive an offer, it may be unconditional or conditional on achieving certain results. Read the terms of your offer carefully. To accept, follow the instructions in the portal and pay the acceptance deposit by the date stated. If you do not respond by the deadline, the offer may be withdrawn and given to another applicant.

Scholarships and financial support

The university offers merit-based and need-based scholarships. Merit scholarships are awarded automatically to applicants with outstanding academic records. Need-based scholarships require a separate application with supporting financial documents. Scholarship decisions are communicated separately from admission decisions.

Students may also be eligible for government scholarships, education loans and part-time campus employment. The financial aid office can help you understand your options and complete the necessary forms.

Contacting the admissions office

If you have questions about your application, please email the admissions office and include your application number in the subject line. The office is open from Monday to Friday, and most enquiries receive a reply within three working days. Please do not submit multiple applications for the same programme, as this may delay the processing of your form.

We look forward to receiving your application and wish you every success.
